sections.title: Executive summary
sections.text: Insufficient evidence for a reliable diagnosis. Review the recorded observations and investigation limitations.

sections.title: Observed evidence
sections.text:
Campaign performance versus baseline and peers: 5 campaign(s) analysed over 30 h ending 2026-10-05T12:00:00.000Z: CTR 0.33%, spend £625.83, 10 attributed orders, CPA £62.58, ROAS 1.64. Versus baseline: CTR -82.5%, hourly spend +27.2%, hourly attributed orders -56.5%. Observations are simulated ad-platform records; frequency and CTR describe exposure and response, not intent.

Sessions, conversion and checkout failures: 787 sessions and 20 orders over 30 h ending 2026-10-05T12:00:00.000Z (conversion 2.54%); 0 checkout failures (0.00% of sessions). Baseline: conversion 2.16% (+17.7% change), failures per hour n/a change, sessions per hour -46.9% change. Simulated storefront records; device and channel slices join orders to their canonical session.

Revenue, orders and conversion versus baseline: Over 30 h ending 2026-10-05T12:00:00.000Z: 20 orders, net revenue £1944.54, 787 sessions, conversion 2.54%. Baseline (30 h): hourly revenue -46.9% change, hourly orders -37.5%, hourly sessions -46.9%. Decomposition: sessions share 0.998, conversion share -0.257, AOV share 0.259 of the revenue change. Values are simulated business records; this describes what changed, not why.

sections.title: Competing explanations
sections.text:
unknown (weak): The available evidence does not justify a reliable causal conclusion.

ad fatigue (weak): Higher average exposure frequency coincides with substantially lower CTR and fewer attributed sessions. This is consistent with audience or creative fatigue across the affected campaigns, but frequency and CTR alone do not establish that mechanism or rule out changes in campaign mix, delivery, or measurement.

ad inefficiency (weak): The campaign aggregate shows weaker click response and acquisition performance alongside greater hourly spend and impressions and fewer attributed sessions and orders per hour. This supports a broad deterioration in paid-ad performance, but does not identify whether fatigue, delivery settings, traffic mix, or measurement caused it.

checkout failure (weak): A checkout problem is not supported by the supplied observations: checkout failures were not recorded, and overall conversion was above baseline. This makes checkout failure an unlikely explanation for the reported paid-ad deterioration, though aggregate conversion cannot rule out an isolated campaign or device segment.
